title: Steak Pizzaiola
description: In Italy, the briefly cooked fresh tomato sauce called pizzaiola is traditionally served atop steak. We use sirloin, but if you'd prefer to use flank steak or skirt steak, just reduce the cooking time. The sauce is also good on pasta.
ingredients: 1 1/4 pounds boneless sirloin steak (about 1 inch thick), excess fat trimmed
1 large onion, sliced 1/4 inch thick (optional but preferred)
2 bell peppers (1 red, 1 yellow), sliced 1/2 inch thick (optional)
4 jarred pepperoncini, drained and thinly sliced (optional)
1 15-ounce can crushed or diced tomatoes (or fresh ones)
directions: Sprinkle the steak all over with 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the steak and sear until browned, about 2 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Add the garlic to the skillet. Once it sizzles, add the onion and bell peppers and cook, stirring occasionally, until they soften slightly, about 4 minutes.

Add the pepperoncini, tomatoes, oregano, red pepper flakes and 3/4 cup water (or red wine) and stir to combine. Bring to a rapid simmer, then nestle the steak in the sauce and simmer, turning once, until medium rare, about 2 to 7 minutes, depending on the thickness of the steak.
Transfer the steak to a cutting board and let rest about 5 minutes.
Continue simmering the sauce until thickened, about 3 more minutes.
Thinly slice the steak against the grain and divide among plates. Top with the sauce and parsley.
